questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion ship a large catalog of predefined BI Publisher reports across financial modules?
options: So consultants never have to log into the application
So a consultant rarely needs to build an entirely new data model and template from a blank page for common, recurring needs
Because custom reports are not technically possible
Predefined reports are only provided for Payables
questions.explain: Oracle ships predefined reports covering common needs so most real-world work is configuring or lightly customizing existing reports, not building from scratch.

questions.q: What does the Payables Invoice Aging Report do?
options: Lists depreciation schedules for fixed assets
Lists unpaid invoices grouped into aging periods
Generates customer account statements
Schedules Enterprise Scheduler Service jobs
questions.explain: The Payables Invoice Aging Report lists unpaid invoices according to specified aging periods, directly answering "what's overdue" questions.

questions.q: Which predefined report type is associated with Receivables rather than Payables or Fixed Assets?
options: Asset Register
Payables-to-Ledger Reconciliation report
Customer statements and an invoice register
Prepayments report
questions.explain: Receivables' predefined reports include aging reports, customer statements, an invoice register, and a receipts register.

questions.q: When a predefined report is close but not quite right for a client's needs, what is the recommended approach?
options: Edit the Oracle-seeded original directly, with no copy kept
Copy the predefined report's template and modify the copy, preserving the ability to fall back to the seeded version
Delete the predefined report entirely and start over with a new data model
Switch the entire report to OTBI instead
questions.explain: Copying the template before modifying it keeps the change auditable and preserves a fallback to Oracle's original seeded report.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect forward to Chapter 6 of the course?
options: Chapter 6 repeats the exact same mechanics content
Chapter 6 covers the content/substance of specific reports like Trial Balance and AP/AR aging, building on the mechanics learned in Chapter 4
Chapter 6 is unrelated to BI Publisher reports
Chapter 6 only covers OTBI, not BI Publisher
questions.explain: Chapter 4 taught the mechanics of BI Publisher; Chapter 6 revisits many of the same reports from the perspective of what they mean in a real close process.
